artworks.what_we_see: Two lifeless gladiators are dragged across a dim, cavernous arena floor by Roman soldiers, while onlookers react in the shadows. The scene is heavy with somber, earthen tones and dramatic light.
artworks.our_interpretation: Many Filipino historians read the painting as an allegory for colonial suffering: the gladiators standing in for the Filipino people, exploited and discarded under foreign rule.
artworks.why_we_chose_it: Spoliarium is one of the most recognized Filipino artworks in history and a natural starting point for a trail celebrating art with deep cultural roots.
artworks.personal_analysis: What strikes us most is the restraint in the color palette against the violence of the subject. It asks the viewer to sit with discomfort rather than look away, which feels like the whole point.

artworks.artwork_title: CAN I TAKE YOUR ORDER PLEASE?
artworks.what_we_see: The painting features a portrait of a humanoid figure. Its head is shaped like a cassette tape with a yellow and red casing labeled “TDK” and “C90” along the bottom front of the casing. The cassette has two large cartoon eyes, and its glasses are made from teal magnetic tape film spilling out from inside the cassette. On top of the cassette rests a small burger topped with a tiny red cap. The figure's body appears to be a connected segmented tube, with red strands of magnetic tape spilling out and looping down toward the shoulders. The figure wears a red and gray collared work shirt/jacket with a small red-and-yellow striped shoulder patch and a tiny embroidered logo of a mascot on the chest. The background is a simple landscape: blue sky with two clouds, distant purple hills, a yellow/green striped field, and two small dark trees.
artworks.our_interpretatio: The painting can be read as a surrealist image of a fast food worker. From the Yum burger that is placed on top of its head to the recognizable Jollibee uniform and logo, the figure is supposed to be an embodiment of an employee in the fast food industry. By turning the head into a cassette tape, it raises different interpretations that bear the same essence. It goes to show how workers in the customer service industry are often seen as replaceable, as every day they repeat the same routine, say the same things to please the masses. In this artwork however, the cassette tape has its magnetic tape spilling out, suggesting exhaustion and burnout. While the bright colors and cartoonish eyes give it a playful look at first, underneath it expresses tiredness and the loss of individuality that comes with repetitive service work.
artworks.our_judgement: The artwork was able to successfully express the social message it was trying to convey by simply making the right choice in choosing what object to use in delivering the metaphor. The usage of the cassette tape as a narrative device was smart and original as it is usually an object that is used to record and playback audio. While being an unusual comparison, putting the two together undoubtedly showcases the similarities.  What makes this effective is the playful style that was chosen in creating the artwork. At first glance, it pulls the viewer in with its bright colors and, yet the small details unveil the truth piece by piece.
artworks.personal_analysis: The painting is defined by contrasting lines. Harsh geometric lines form the cassette's rectangular shape and internal divisions, while soft organic strokes define the rest of the figure, such as the spilling magnetic tape and the folds of the shirt. This contrast carries over into shape. The head is composed of geometric forms like the rectangular cassette and circular eyes and glasses, while the body is rendered with softer organic forms that highlight the duality between mechanical and human. The artist also uses warm cool color contrast, where the warm orange red shirt and tan bun stand out against the cool blue sky and teal glasses, which separates the figure from the background. Texture varies from the smooth glossy surface of the cassette to the woven fabric of the shirt and the soft matte bun. The centered and symmetrical composition creates a stable portrait-like presence despite its surreal subject, with emphasis placed on the cartoonish eyes as the only lifelike feature. Finally, the flat minimal background provides negative space that isolates the figure and allows it to dominate the frame.

artworks.what_we_see: The sculpture is composed of small wooden houses stacked together that are sticking out in different angles. The individual houses vary in colors such as teal, orange, yellow, pink, blue, mint green, purple, brown, gray and white while the roof of each home is painted in neutral colors such as black, brown and beige. The whole structure rests on thin metal rod supports mounted to a wooden rectangular base, which bears an engraved/carved signature.
artworks.our_interpretation: The sculpture evokes the feeling of a densely packed neighbourhood, a community that was not created with a plan but rather built over time and on a whim, which is why the houses are scattered on the hillside. The whole sculpture being held by thin rods instead of a solid base suggests the fragility and instability of the community, hinting at the vulnerability of its situation. It feels like a nod to the neighbourhoods in the Philippines, how some communities often found themselves jammed together in an attempt to make do with what they have, even if it means enduring cramped conditions just to have a place to stay. As Filipinos are commonly described to be resilient, this artwork becomes an extension of the struggles such communities face in their day-to-day life. The fragile base shows how uncertain life can be in these communities, while the bright colors and lively arrangement show their energy and togetherness.
artworks.our_judgement: The sculpture was able to invoke the feeling of familiarity from the get go.Its composition is strikingly similar to neighbourhoods found in rural cities, transforming a common sight into a visually thoughtful form that pushes the audience to reflect on the social reality it implies. The tightly packed houses feel almost suffocating, yet the vibrant colors suggest otherwise. It used the right palette to highlight the contrast between harsh reality and community resilience. It takes a lot of creativity and skill to make a piece look intentionally unbalanced, and the thin metal rods show the technical ability needed to balance it on an unstable pole. It is impactful because it shifts the focus from hardship to the adaptability and resourcefulness of informal communities
artworks.personal_analysis: The sculpture is made from the repetition of a single form, a small rectangular house module varied in size, roofline and tilt. The differences within similar subjects create rhythm while preventing monotony. Color helps activate that rhythm. The artist distributes bright contrasting hues like teal, magenta, orange, yellow and mint across the individual houses, which guides the eye and creates a sense of movement throughout the piece. The sculpture is balanced in a way that feels unstable. The large grouping of houses extends outward from a narrow central column and is supported only by thin metal rods rather than a solid base. This contrast between the heavy appearance of the wooden forms and the thinness of the supports beneath them makes the whole structure feel delicate and as if it could fall. There is no single focal point, so the arrangement emphasizes density and accumulation

artworks.what_we_see: A seated woman in muted traditional dress, gazing just past the viewer, hands folded in her lap.
artworks.our_interpretation: A quiet study of motherhood and patience, painted with unusual tenderness for its era.
artworks.why_we_chose_it: It's one of the few portraits in the trail painted by a woman artist, and it shows.
artworks.personal_analysis: The gaze never quite meets yours, which somehow makes the portrait feel more honest, not less.

artworks.what_we_see: A weathered farmer's face rendered in bold, confident charcoal strokes, half in shadow.
artworks.our_interpretation: A tribute to the agricultural roots still visible on Santa Rosa's outskirts, even as the city grows upward.
artworks.why_we_chose_it: It grounds the trail in the people who worked this land long before the malls arrived.
artworks.personal_analysis: The shadow half of the face is the part we kept coming back to — it feels like it's hiding a whole life story.

artworks.what_we_see: Layered paper cutouts of birds mid-flight, collaged over a soft gradient sky.
artworks.our_interpretation: A hopeful piece about movement and change, fitting for a city in transition.
artworks.why_we_chose_it: Its mixed-media texture stands out from the mostly flat paintings elsewhere on the trail.
artworks.personal_analysis: We like that it doesn't try to be photorealistic — the cut edges of the paper are part of the charm.

about.group_introduction: We are a group of students documenting the art hiding in plain sight around Santa Rosa, Laguna — from museum-grade works to pieces made by our own neighbors.
about.why_we_created_statement: We built this trail because so much local art goes unlabeled and unexplained. We wanted a place where a painting on a barangay hall wall gets the same care and context as something hanging in a museum.
